findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - running the scheduled Linux starter-smoke job.
The proof compares isolated installs at 17.01 and 5.57 seconds, but explicitly reports no before-and-after timing for the starter-smoke job. It therefore does not establish the requested job-level improvement. The pull-request workflow also excludes these changed test files from its trigger (.github/workflows/starter-smoke.yml:7-11), so a pending PR check will not supply that measurement.
findings.title: Not done: The smoke fixtures share downloaded packages while keeping separate app copies, and the starter smoke job is measurably faster

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a smoke run uses separate stores after a fixture configuration regression.
No suite test checks that the two actual fixtures reuse downloads while retaining separate app copies. The named lint test requests only lint_starter (tests/test_libs_layout.py:209-220), and the live starter test checks application results, not reuse (tests/test_starter_tree.py:519-522). Restoring either fixture's private store would therefore pass those checks. The three-copy measurement is a one-off check, and the reported 103-test run had live smoke disabled. An executable regression check needs to exercise the fixture behavior and fail when reuse or app separation breaks.
findings.title: Gate: smoke-fixture download reuse

stop.reason: Harm 3 or higher findings: one more round by the standing rule

why: Forge's starter smoke lint fixture installs every package again in its own store, adding minutes to a 35-minute job
